head: 6c7b8436d9591546f9b89f74c366536aafd8ce51
summary:
SL-068 changes only documentation and adds one check script. The decision record's numbers hold up when re-run.
- **Release, 100,000-child read:** 9.08-14.54 ms against 250 ms (34/34 tests).
- **Default suite:** 381/381, run in Debug. The timing test ran in it at 20.62-24.07 ms.
- **Check script:** SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1 exits 0 for All and for C-001..C-005 run one by one.
- **Fitness:** all 62 rules hold.
- **Real temp NTFS tree scanned through the built Core dll:** an empty folder gives 0 rows, a single child gives 1 row at share 1.0, and tied sizes come out largest first then in listing order, the same on a second read.
- **Window case T-003 on the published exe, run twice, both passed.** Run 2: cold open 100.6 ms at the default window (sort 48.2) and 100.4 ms in the tall window (sort 47.1). Run 1, tall window: 237.0 ms (sort 43.9, the rest 185.1). The non-sort share the build flagged (162.5 ms) is run-to-run noise, not a trend.

The two obligations owed to validate are discharged.
- **O-001:** git cannot show the rule came first. The rule and the figures both first appear in b5c2b62. The ledger dates design 29 before build 1, design-29 holds the rule and only an estimate with no measured figure, and the doc says all of this.
- **O-002:** the trip wire runs unattended. The timing test has no Trait and no Skip, the default filter keeps it, and the default run is Debug.

**It is not a pass, for two reasons:**
- The three fixes owed to build-slice (O-011, O-012, O-013) were never made. Build ran once, before code review, and the doc still has lines 42, 59 and 70-71 as they were. As a result, planned item 4 is graded no. I confirmed m1 and m2 against the tree. In m1 the doc gets the origin of the brief's 9-40 ms wrong: SL-042's reflection wrote it on 2026-09-26 by joining 9.16-9.80 and 35.9-40.2. In m2, FolderTreeNode keeps each opened folder's rows until the next scan, so "nothing is kept per folder" is wrong for the window. O-013 is only partly right: the engine's own record lists SL-042 spike verdicts, and the replacement text code review prescribed would itself mix two memory measures.
- The slice's first deliverable, the engine's Scan Store line reading sort-on-read, is outside this worktree. The build reports it not applied, so I could not check it.

The planned field holds at most 7 entries, so items 1-7 are graded there and items 8-11 are graded in criteria as 'Planned item N'. No loop: every stage ran once.

checks.what: O-001: did the rule arrive in git before the figures?
checks.command: git log -S 'Children are sorted on read, never stored' / -S '35.9 to 40.2 ms' -- docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md; git log --diff-filter=A -- .taad/slices/SL-042/design-slice-29.json
checks.evidence: All three first appear in b5c2b62 (2026-09-26 05:43:57 +0530), so git cannot order the rule before the result. SL-068 doc :22-25 says exactly that.

checks.what: O-001: ledger order and the content of SL-042's design-29
checks.command: ConvertFrom-Json .taad/slices/SL-042/index.json; read design-slice-29.json lines 58, 136-138; Select-String '35.9|40.2|9.16|9.80' on design-slice-29.json
checks.evidence: The ledger has design-slice #29 at 2026-09-25 17:23:45Z and build-slice #1 at 23:47:34Z. Line 136 holds 'Sort children on every read ... store no per-folder order'. Line 138 says 'The estimate is tens of milliseconds' and 'If the test fails, a cached order can sit behind the same call'. No measured figure appears in the file.

checks.what: O-002: Trait, Skip and default Configuration of the timing test
checks.command: Grep Trait|Skip|Collection|Configuration in ScanStoreRollupTimingTests.cs; Grep Configuration|VSTestTestCaseFilter in Directory.Build.*, *.csproj, eng/dotnet.ps1, global.json, *.runsettings
checks.evidence: The test has no Trait and no Skip, and has [Collection(nameof(MemoryBudget))] at :14. The default filter is Network!=TEST-NET-1&Network!=SMB-LOOPBACK&Cloud!=CF-SYNC-ROOT (csproj :13-14). No file sets a default Configuration.

checks.what: Default Core suite with no filter and no -c (O-002 trip wire, and the regression check)
checks.evidence: Exit 0; 381 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. The trx has the timing test Passed, stdout 'Debug build ... 20.62, 20.76, 24.07, 20.70, 23.03, 21.22, 23.79, 21.02, 22.50, 21.97; slowest 24.07, budget 250'. The trx folder was removed afterwards.

checks.what: Release: ScanStore and ArchitectureRules tests, including the 100,000-child timing test
checks.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests -c Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ScanStore|FullyQualifiedName~ArchitectureRules" --logger "console;verbosity=detailed"

checks.what: The slice's own check script, all cases
checks.evidence: Exit 0, 'every check held'. C-006, C-007 and C-008 lines all ok, including 'nothing under src/ changed' and 'no fitness rule's files glob reaches either document'.

checks.what: Check script cases C-001..C-005 run one by one
checks.evidence: Each exit 0. C-002 covers the handed, edited, reworded and doubled lines. C-003: numstat 2 0 and lines 1-127 byte-identical. C-004: the range equals the min/max of the listed reads. C-004 does not catch the m1 origin error: it only looks for '9-40' on a line containing 'brief'.

checks.what: Criterion 9 on a real temp NTFS tree through the built Release Core dll
checks.command: throwaway pwsh script in %TEMP%\sl068-val-*: tree\{empty, one\only.bin 20000 B, ties\a..d.bin 12288 B + z-big.bin 40960 B}; Scanner.Scan; ChildrenLargestFirst on each folder, twice; remove temp in finally
checks.evidence: status=Completed files=6 folders=3. empty: count=0. one: count=1 [only.bin:20480:1.000]. ties: [z-big.bin:40960:0.455, a.bin, b.bin, c.bin, d.bin at 12288 and 0.136 each]. Second read identical in all three. Temp removed.

checks.what: Window case T-003 on the published exe, run 1
checks.evidence: PASSED: T-003, exit 0. Tall window: cold open 237.0 ms (sort 43.9, rows 7.2, the rest 185.1), 46 rows built, first row the largest file; warm opens 1.7-4.0 ms. My output filter dropped this run's default-window cold figure.

checks.what: Window case T-003 on the published exe, run 2 (the second measurement the build asked for)
checks.evidence: PASSED: T-003, exit 0. 100,000 files built in 25.5 s. Default window: cold 100.6 ms (sort 48.2, rows 7.4, the rest 44.0). Tall: cold 100.4 ms (sort 47.1, rest 44.6). Across runs 'the rest' swings 44-185 ms: noise. The script removed its own temp tree, and no FsAnalyser.App process was left.
62 rules checked against 100 parsed files: every declared rule holds.

checks.what: The pointer in the SL-042 doc, and what code, test, eng and fitness paths the slice touched
checks.command: git diff 6566536 HEAD -- docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md; git diff --numstat ...; git diff --name-only 6566536 HEAD -- src .taad/fitness.yaml tests eng
checks.evidence: The SL-042 doc gains two lines after :126 (the pointer and a blank line); numstat '2 0'. Under src, tests, eng and fitness.yaml the only path is the new tests/bugs/SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1.

checks.what: Does anything run tests/bugs scripts automatically?
checks.evidence: No matches. The script is only run by hand, so its fixed-line checks cannot break a default run.

checks.what: O-011 (m1): origin of the brief's 9-40 ms
checks.command: Grep '9-40|9\.16|9\.80|136 MiB|96 MiB' in .taad/slices/SL-042; Read doc :40-42
checks.evidence: Doc :42 still says 'The slice's brief rounded this to 9-40 ms' (this = the 2026-09-28 runs). SL-042 reflect-1.json:74 and index.json:153 wrote '9-40 ms' on 2026-09-26, joining validate-slice-1.json:176 (9.16-9.80) with the build's 35.9-40.2. Finding stands, unfixed.

Doc :59 is unchanged. FolderTreeNode.cs:15-16: children are 'built once as rows and put in Children whole ... and kept until the next scan'. :142-158 stores them. T-003 opens 2-5 are 'warm, reusing them'.

checks.what: O-013 (R2-m3): '136 MiB of headroom SL-042's spike measured'
checks.command: Read doc :69-71; SL-042 index.json risk-spike stage; SL-042 reflect-1.json:84; SL-042 doc :81-84
checks.evidence: Doc :70-71 is unchanged, so the obligation still stands. Its premise is contested: the engine's record lists [SL-042] spike verdicts, including 'HashSet<UInt128> peak 887.8 MiB (136 under 1 GiB)'. The prescribed '96 MiB retained' mixes a GC-heap delta (555.8 to 652.1) with a private-bytes headroom. SL-044's spike measured as-built peak private at 816 MiB max.

checks.what: Search for the engine's architecture record in this worktree
checks.command: Get-ChildItem .taad (excluding slices); git grep -n -i 'sorted largest first' -- ':!.taad/slices'
checks.evidence: .taad holds only fitness.yaml. The old clause appears only in SL-042 doc :122, SL-068 doc :3/:112 and the check script's fixtures. No record file and no stand-in.

checks.what: Read the engine's actual Scan Store architecture line
checks.evidence: The record is not in this worktree, no tool this stage holds reads or writes it, and the brief does not show it. The build reports the edit 'not applied'. No listed elevation reaches it.

criteria.criterion: Slice criterion 1: the engine's recorded Scan Store architecture line reads sort-on-read instead of 'stored sorted largest first'
criteria.how: The record is outside this worktree and unreadable from here. The build reports 'not applied' (doc :105) and leaves the find/replace text. Whether validate may pass with this unknown is an open design question for a person, and it is not answered.

criteria.criterion: Slice criterion 2: the sort-on-read question is closed, recorded as decided on the measured numbers
criteria.how: Doc :61-71 records 'Decision: closed'. Its Core figures match the recorded runs (C-004), and my Release (9.08-14.54 ms) and Debug default (20.62-24.07 ms) runs fall inside its claims. The record still carries three uncorrected factual errors (O-011/O-012/O-013).

criteria.criterion: Planned item 8: a docs-only diff leaves the code and tests alone
criteria.how: Nothing under src/, no existing test and not .taad/fitness.yaml changed (git diff --name-only). Fitness holds 62/62, and no files glob reaches either doc (C-008). Literally, the diff also adds tests/bugs/SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1, which reads docs/design. The build declared that deviation (O-003..O-010 required a runnable check per case), and code review accepted it. Nothing in eng, the csproj, the slnx or the window scripts runs the script (grep: no matches).

criteria.criterion: Planned item 9: a 100,000-child folder's children read largest first, including an empty folder, a single child and tied sizes
criteria.how: Real temp NTFS tree through the Release Core dll: empty gives 0 rows; single gives 1 row at share 1.000; with ties, z-big 40960 comes first, then a, b, c, d in listing order, and repeat reads are identical. The unit tests and the 100k timing test passed (34/34 Release, 381/381 default). T-003 twice: 100,000 rows, first row the largest file.

criteria.criterion: Planned item 10: a reopen is judged from a timing number (one slow Release run under load, or a Debug run over 250 ms)
criteria.how: Doc :86-87 says a single slow run is re-run once and reopens only if it holds, and that 'A Debug number does not reopen it'. Doc :99 says 'only a Release run counts toward 1'. The test logs its configuration (my trx stdout begins 'Debug build').

criteria.criterion: Planned item 11: the Scan Store budget figures are stated when the engine line's 699 MiB/572 MB differ from the as-built store
criteria.how: Doc :80-82 names 699 MiB and 572 MB, cites the as-built 652.1 MiB retained (SL-042 doc :81-84), and disclaims re-auditing them. The submitted edit keeps the budget figures (:119). The separate headroom sentence at :70-71 is O-013, still open.

planned.evidence: No write path exists, and the doc handles that as the design's fallback requires. It says 'Status: **not applied**', gives the reason, and labels its wording submitted text, not a copy of the record (:103-108). C-001 exits 0. git grep shows 'No child order is stored' only in the doc and the check script, and no architecture-record file was added.

The find/replace applies only when the old clause occurs exactly once; otherwise it applies nothing and reports the text found (doc :110-119). C-002 exits 0 with 15 checks across the handed, edited, reworded and doubled lines.

git diff 6566536..HEAD: the SL-042 doc gains +2 lines after :126 (the pointer at :128 and a blank line), numstat '2 0'. At base, line 127 is blank and line 128 is the next heading. C-003 exits 0: lines 1-127 are byte-identical and the rest is shifted by two lines.

The numbers themselves are right and kept harness by harness: range 8.84-44.12 = the listed reads' min/max, SL-044 figures match its doc :127-130, and no range spans the two harnesses (C-004 exit 0). But doc :42 misstates where the brief's 9-40 ms came from. SL-042 reflect-1.json:74 (2026-09-26) joined validate's 9.16-9.80 (validate-slice-1.json:176) and the build's 35.9-40.2. It was not a rounding of the 2026-09-28 runs. That is the exact case this item names, and the O-011 fix was never applied.

Doc :22-25 says the ledger dates the rule first and that git shows rule and result together in b5c2b62. Both are verified: git log -S puts line 45, the line 88 figures and design-slice-29.json all in b5c2b62; the ledger has design #29 at 17:23:45Z and build #1 at 23:47:34Z; design-29 holds the rule with only an 'estimate'. The doc names SL-042's design as author and leaves the override to the person.

The test has no Trait and no Skip, and the default filter keeps it. No default Configuration is set, so the default run is Debug. My default run passed 381/381 with the timing test in Debug (20.62-24.07 ms). Doc :86-101 says this and names T-003, which fails at >=500 ms, as the window guard; I ran T-003 twice and it passed both times.

'## Not covered' (:73-79) excludes re-sorting during a live refresh, citing SL-044's 84 ms against 50 and 866 against 250 (C-007 checks this against SL-044 doc :17-19). The decision limits itself to a completed store and a cold open (:69). The Memory bullet at :59 separately misstates window state (O-012, unfixed), which would mislead the same live-refresh reader.

obligations.evidence: git cannot show it: SL-042 doc line 45, the line 88 figures and design-slice-29.json all first appear in b5c2b62. The ledger does show it: design #29 at 2026-09-25T17:23:45Z, build #1 at 23:47:34Z, and design-29:136-138 holds the rule with only an 'estimate' and no measured figure. The obligation's fallback holds: the doc (:22-25) says they arrived together in git and quotes both ledger times.

ScanStoreRollupTimingTests has no Trait and no Skip, the default VSTestTestCaseFilter keeps it, and no default Configuration is set, so the default run is Debug. My no-filter, no -c run exited 0 with 381/381, and the trx shows the timing test Passed with 'Debug build ... slowest 24.07, budget 250'. The doc says only a Release run reopens the question.

Owed to build-slice and never applied: build ran once (6c7b843), before code review, and doc :42 still says 'The slice's brief rounded this to 9-40 ms'. The finding is verified. SL-042 reflect-1.json:74 and index.json:153 wrote '9-40 ms' on 2026-09-26, from validate-slice-1.json:176 (9.16-9.80) joined with the build's 35.9-40.2. Send back to build-slice.

Owed to build-slice and never applied: doc :59 still says 'Nothing is kept per folder.' The finding is verified. FolderTreeNode.cs:15-16 says children are 'built once as rows and put in Children whole ... and kept until the next scan', EnsureChildren (:142-158) stores the ordered nodes, and my T-003 opens 2-5 are 'warm, reusing them'. Send back to build-slice.

Owed to build-slice and never applied: doc :70-71 is unchanged. The finding's premise is partly wrong, and its prescribed fix should not be applied as written. The engine's record lists [SL-042] spike verdicts ('HashSet<UInt128> peak 887.8 MiB (136 under 1 GiB)'), which contradicts 'SL-042 ran no spike'; the SL-042 index only shows risk-spike 'passed' with attempts []. The prescribed '96 MiB retained' is a GC-heap delta (555.8 to 652.1 MiB, SL-042 doc :82-84) applied to a private-bytes headroom; SL-044's spike measured as-built peak private at 816 MiB max (about 208 MiB under 1 GiB). The real flaw is quoting a throwaway layout's headroom as current. Build-slice should fix the sentence against the as-built measurement, and code review should settle the wording.

not_reached: The engine's architecture record: whether its Scan Store line now reads sort-on-read. It is outside this worktree, no stage has a read or write path to it, and it is not an elevation matter.
The person's decision on the design's open question: may validate pass with slice criterion 1 unknown, or must the edit be seen in the record? Unanswered, and not mine to decide.
Behaviour during a live, mid-scan refresh (SL-044 NO-GO): out of this slice's scope and not measured here.
The default-window cold-open figure from my first T-003 run: my output filter dropped it. The second run captured both window sizes.
Whether the three doc fixes (O-011/O-012/O-013) are applied correctly: they were never attempted, so there is nothing to check yet.
